text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Youth job plan sidesteps training: Ottawa effort stresses work experience to avoid clash with provincial services.
- RCMP to probe loss of blood files: Police have started initial inquiry.
- Ontario tuition to rise by up to 10 percent: Education Minister John Snobelen's announcement also means deeper debt for some postsecondary students.
- Demons return to haunt Argentina: Murder, corruption rear ugly heads.
- Chief finds free trip to China has its costs: Boothby has second thoughts about accepting invitation.
- Plugged Peel courts caught in paper chase: Even Crown attorney calls prosecution over missing 50-cent Toronto tabloid a waste of time.
- Merger forms securities giant: C$10-billion deal joining Dean Witter and Morgan Stanley shakes up global industry.
- Investors renew love affair with real estate: Sparked by commercial sector revival.
- Toyota plans C$400-million retooling of Ontario plant: Auto firm to produce 50,000 sport coupes at Cambridge.
- Peter Pocklington plans to take Edmonton Oilers public: Will apply share proceeds to ATB loan.
- Canadian banks get jitters as new giant walks Wall Street: Dean Witter to merge with Morgan Stanley in US$10.1-billion deal to create financial services powerhouse.
- Toyota pumps C$430-million into Canada-made couple.
